Rules / Cleanup

SK0261 The attribute writes out what the language already supplies

An attribute written with the Attribute suffix the language appends for you, or an [AttributeUsage] argument that restates that attribute's own default.

CategoryCleanup
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesRedundantAttributeUsageProperty

Why

[SerializableAttribute] and [Serializable] are the same attribute, and the suffix is the part the language was designed to let you leave out — writing it makes a reader check whether this is the type they know under the short name. Inherited = true and AllowMultiple = false are worse than noise: they are the defaults written out, so a reader who has learned to read the argument list as "the decisions this attribute made" is handed two decisions that were never taken. ⚠ Both are shapes a model reaches for, because the fully-spelled form is what the framework reference documentation shows.

Example

Instead of:

[SerializableAttribute]
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class, Inherited = true, AllowMultiple = false)]
class MarkerAttribute : Attribute { }

Write:

[Serializable]
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class)]
class MarkerAttribute : Attribute { }

The ReSharper mapping

⚠ Two ReSharper inspections, one concept: RedundantAttributeSuffix (a warning) and RedundantAttributeUsageProperty (a suggestion). Skala reports the concept at warning.

⚠ Neither is hosted, and both zeros are verified rather than assumed. Reflecting over SDK 10.0.400's analyzer assemblies gives 440 descriptors and none of them is either shape; a probe with all 120 IDE ids forced to warning, AnalysisMode=All and AnalysisLevel=latest-all reported nothing on [SerializableAttribute] or on Inherited = true, on a compilation where IDE0055, IDE0161, IDE0100, IDE0075 and IDE0380 all fired and no AD0001 was raised. Neither shape is a compiler warning either.

When it does not fire

⚠ The suffix is only droppable when nothing answers to the short name, and that is a lookup rather than a string operation. [FooAttribute] resolves to FooAttribute, but [Foo] searches for both Foo and FooAttribute — so a type named Foo anywhere in scope changes what the shortened attribute means, or makes it CS1614 when both are attribute classes. The rule asks LookupNamespacesAndTypes for the short name at the attribute's own position and withdraws the finding if anything at all comes back, which is deliberately stricter than the language: a non-attribute Foo beside an attribute FooAttribute is in fact still unambiguous, and is declined anyway, because "is the other candidate an attribute class" is a second question and getting it wrong changes which type is applied. ⚠ The shortened name must also still be an identifier. A type may legally be called voidAttribute; [void] is a parse error, so SyntaxFacts.GetKeywordKind is asked before the edit is offered. ⚠ Only a simple name is reported. A qualified [System.SerializableAttribute] carries a second redundancy in the qualifier, which is SK0243's span and its concept; leaving the qualified form to that rule keeps one node from being rewritten by two ids in one pass. ⚠ The `[AttributeUsage]` half checks the attribute's identity, not its name. A user-written AttributeUsageAttribute in another namespace has whatever defaults it declares, so the shape is reported only against System.AttributeUsageAttribute. ⚠ The deleted span runs from the end of the preceding argument so that the separating comma goes with it, and it is that span — never the node — that is asked about comments and directives, which is the defect #302 describes.
